interactions.title: Riswynn’s maps and the hidden exit
lines: Riswynn: Well, since you are a cartographer, and that sparked my memory, I realized I haven’t shown you the maps that I—that my uncle drew. And they don't create any landmarks for me to follow, but perhaps with your slight familiarity with the region, something could come to mind.
DM: So this is—you're talking about this. You've now camped for the night after your first day of travel, and Riswynn brings out these two maps.
Kenzo: How large is Raven's Hold? The whole, the whole complex?
DM: None of you have ever been there.
Kenzo: But based on these maps, we have a…
Riswynn: Based on our history, it was a significant trading post of multiple races, so I'm thinking fairly substantial.
Wellby: Like a flash of the image.

DM: Oh yeah, so I guess between all that, you know, it's probably—you know, this like outer wall might be half a mile across, right? And you're talking this whole sort of valley area is, you know, maybe a mile by three—you know, a mile by a half mile in area. So, you know…

DM: Not insubstantial. The fortress itself? Hard to say. None of you really know. It would have been home to, you know, something like, you know, 100 dwarves at any one time, with space for markets and mining and crafting as well, and…
Kenzo: Underground, who knows how big it is.
DM: This would be that. So the—there's like the dwarves in… The castle is the Dunmari outpost, and then the river, and the dwarves and caves are on the other side.
DM: The, the Dunmari fortress and the dwarven outpost are across the valley from each other.
Kenzo: So this is the human side. This is the Dunmari side.
DM: Yeah, the castle, on my side on the right.
DM: The big fancy road that goes across that people would, you know…
Delwath: Back and forth on before the war. Where all the vines and various other deadly things…
DM: I mean, Ander got past the outer wall—the outer wall—but he never got…

Wellby: So the vines—the vines, though we don't know that there's the full extent of it, but we know for sure that just inside that outer wall like where the river flows in, there's like a huge field of them there. So it doesn't guarantee that going through the mines would avoid everything, but we definitely avoid at least that field of vines.
Seeker: There's a note about the secret entrance to the dwarven outpost perhaps being hidden, or maybe booby-trapped. Also marked as hidden exit and entrance.
DM: Right, so it's probably more likely a escape route, rather than have the—right…

DM: Right. So it's a way for the dwarves to just have them have not just one exit, instead of a way for people to get in. But presumably if somebody can go out that somebody can come in as well, right? But like you can have a one-way…
Seeker: I guess you could have a one-way…

Riswynn: That's why I wasn't thinking of it as a entrance. We wouldn't know how to find it to begin with, but also my mindset was just that of the sort of custom, that it was an escape route, an exit, and not… I'm all for repurposing things to make them useful, but not sure about our prospects of getting in that way.

before: Delwath: Now, I think, the sooner we get there, the better.
Riswynn: And if we run into any on the road when we're crossing it, or if we take it for a little ways, they'll be closer to whatever has happened, so they'll have fresher news.

Wellby: The thing I've been thinking of with Raven’s Hold, this, this, this, there's this back entrance into it right from underground from the dwarven mines, there's some way for me to be looking at the two dwarves, wondering, do you know how to do…
Unknown: That?
Seeker: Reasonable question.
after: Seeker: And the next post north on that long road north might be hundreds of miles to the north.
DM: It could be, yes.
Wellby: Off ramps every couple of miles, or…
Unknown: Something.
Seeker: So then there's the seal ourselves up in barrels at the top of the waterfall approach.

interactions.title: Agreeing on Wellby’s spyglass purchase
lines: Kenzo: This might be a touch of a retcon, Tim, but I feel like we're going to be traveling on all these grassy—these plains and the desert, and like it's all this flatland. You got to see far ahead. I don't think it'd be so crazy for Wellby to have acquired a spyglass that, you know, if he needed some money for it, Kenzo could have chipped in for.
Kenzo: You some money, some money for spyglass, cuz…
Wellby: I think I have a spyglass here on my character sheet.
DM: Good for you. You've got a spyglass.

DM: I mean, you're not gonna, you know, possibly in Chardon you could acquire a, you know, a fancy spyglass that is, you know, equivalent, perhaps, to like one of Galileo's telescopes or something like that. But, you know, in Karawa, the best you're going to do is, you know, twice their size. Doesn't have to cost 1000, might cost, you know, 50 gold or something like that. But you're not—this is not technology that would be—certainly in Dun—in this part of Dunmar, you would not be having spy glasses all over the place, I think. Ah…
Kenzo: You have enough gold for a spyglass?
DM: I'm, I'm gonna say, I'm gonna say, let's say in Dunmar, it would be, you'd have a spyglass; it would cost you 100 gold.
Wellby: No, I don't have enough gold for a spyglass.

DM: And you're talking about something that's going to, at best, magnify something one and a half time, something like maybe twice, depending on the light. Basically, you're talking about like a leather, you know, some leather tube that you can put like glass in and sort of fiddle with a little bit to get there.
Wellby: What else we spend our money on?
Kenzo: You want, you want, you want some gold?

before: Delwath: But let’s—I mean, it would be good to try and confuse the issue if they’re watching us. You know, we should have brought binoculars. Those are totally invented, right?
DM: You might be able to track down a spyglass, but that would be expensive; wouldn't be something somebody would just give you.

Delwath: I was saying we should try to confuse the—like, we don't want it to be obvious that there's five of us riding horses. Like, if we can—if we can, I mean, they're probably going to notice the horses. But if we can try and make it so that they might not notice how many people there are, right? Like a group of two with five horses wouldn't be particularly surprising.
Riswynn: Mega…
DM: Pack animals. Right, right.
after: DM: So are you—you're at the road, or are you…?
Wellby: Humor me. Look at these things closely again with whatever I'm left with.
DM: So, as they're a mile off, it's definitely people on horseback in the front, being trailed by some sort of small animal, and then there's, you know, some people on foot in the back.
Seeker: How many—do you want us…?
Kenzo: You want to stay ahead? I…

interactions.title: Shani’s flight from fire and gnolls
lines: DM: Ah, ah, the one in the front sees you, obviously, and pulls up her horse and looks quite startled and kind of motions for, you know, for everybody to, to stop in, and she rides forward. And none of them particularly have, you know, weapons or anything. She's carrying, you know, a couple of spears, but they seem, you know, she's not a warrior, right? These are not—none of these are particularly fighters. And she just kind of looks shocked to see you and rides up and just spouts off in Dunmari:
DM: “What? Where? Who—who are you? What are you doing? What are you doing?”
((The companions clarify their position at the horse blind))

Wellby: Just put it on the table, let's say: "My companions and I have been in Karawa this last week, and after a series of attacks, some coming from Raven's Hold, they and I have been traveling to Raven's Hold try and find the source. It looks like you all may have encountered some of the beasts that we saw."

DM: These—I don't know if I'd call these… Creatures came across us in the night. Last night we sacrificed a third of our flock to keep them at bay while we fled. Two of us lost horses. We've heard the land, the entire land east of the river Hara, is lost to us, and…

DM: Were fleeing as fast as we can. Beware if you're heading north. The goats may satisfy them for some time, but they could still be on the road, or off the road. There were six of them, and they seemed—well, malevolent is a nice way to put it. Vicious. Do not want to see those creatures again.
Seeker: So as we ride up, I'll say, "It looks like some of your companions are injured. Can we offer you any of our healing arts?"
DM: If you have healing, we would not say no.

DM: It's—so it's the, the two that lost their horses seemed like they were the ones who are most in need. One of them is not badly off at all. You know, she was scraped up a bit, but doesn't seem to be still bleeding or anything. The other looks like he has a broken arm.
Seeker: I draw a small image of whole, glowing bones in the air, but quickly, so as not to draw too much attention, and gently bestow it upon the arm of the person.

DM: He looks like shocked and happy and says, "Wow." He's like touching his arm like he's—I mean, he's seen healing magic before, but in there—in his experience it's usually this like, like mud stuff that the—you know, the healing mud of Karawa’s locally reasonably well known. But just instantaneous healing without any touch or anything like that, he has not seen before. And it's like looking around: "Wow. Thank you. Thank you, kind dwarf. That's—that's amazing. If only we could bring the horses back."
Seeker: I wish we could do more.
Wellby: Well, where are you coming from for the festival?

DM: We are—we were indeed late for the festival. Good grazing, and there's quite—well, I wouldn't call it bad weather. There's a storm up north that seems like it will never end. Lightning, thunder. And we were caught behind a blaze of fire started by lightning strike, and had to detour quite far east out of our way to this, this road, as the fire was burning across the plains as we were trying to come directly to Karawa.

DM: This lightning storm has been there for a week or more. There's no way that's normal. He's sort of looking at you like—her, she, the one who is the leader—like making sure that, in fact, it's not normal.
Riswynn: Normal—how far from the mountains? Or, or close to the mountains?
DM: So that's this in the map in Roll20. It's this thing right here. So it's in the—it's sort of just south of the mountains, but a good bit west of Raven's Hold.
Wellby: Can get any more detail from them about like size or scale, or like more precise landmarks around it?

DM: Of course, I never rode up to it, but you can see it on the horizon. Once you get in to the point in which you can see the mountains and you look north, you'll see this towering gray cloud that's just hanging over the foothills, and every now and then lightning blast through the sky. But I haven't got any closer to it than maybe 20 miles, but it's visible from quite a distance, and it just looks—it just looks like a thunder storm, but massive—15, 20 miles across, just sitting there on the plains.
Seeker: Do you know what's directly above—like, what's beneath it?
DM: You couldn't pay me enough to live underneath that.
Wellby: How close to Raven’s Hold were you when you made it to the road?
DM: Less than a day’s travel north of here.

Seeker: Oh, since we've encountered some of these demons, as you say, ourselves, and we've seen a few varieties, we're curious what kind you encountered. Can you say more about exactly what they were?

DM: They were—well, I have to admit I didn't get an amazingly good look at them. But they were—they looked almost as if you took a human, took a person, but replaced his head with that of a hyena, jackal. And the rest of its body sort of like a human, except for claws. And some of them were—you know, they have spears; they had weapons.

DM: And when they—when they reached the goats, and we, we slaughtered some of our goats, left them, thinking they look like some kind of hyena beast and maybe they would be distracted. And it did slow them down enough for us to get away. They seemed—they didn't stop and butcher the creatures with their swords or spears; they would just tear into the flesh of the goats as we ran. And I didn't look back at that point.
Kenzo: How many did you say you saw again?
DM: Sorry, six. They surprised us at night, at night. I'm surprised we even got away. I think gods must be watching out for us.
Kenzo: Are they, are they headed south, chasing after you now?
DM: We have not stopped since we ran from them. We've been traveling south since the middle of last night. They may be following. I hope not. I don't know what to say.

Kenzo: So you should know that the entire—that Karawa has fled completely west to Tokra, and all folks traveling in the land and in this area now are all fleeing to safety in Tokra. So from here, there, there are—there are still—there are still some mystai at the temple in Karawa, and they're staying fortified there, so you may be able to find some safety there. You may be able to find some provisions there. Otherwise, the, the main—on—all anybody out right now is moving west to Tokra.

DM: We are planning on turning west in another day or so, once we're more sure of the land. Okay, I am—none of us want to stay here. Now, I had heard that everywhere east of the river is now given over to our enemies. Whether that's true or not, I don't know, but that's—that flows past Tokra.
Wellby: How did you hear that? Where did you go?

DM: From rumors. Who told me that? Two days ago a rider came north. He was—let's see—my mother's sisters cousin-in-law. Looking for us, I believe, as we were late for the festival, and warned us. Was it two days ago? I believe it was two days ago, yes. Now the time blurs together. It's been nearly—well, barely slept last night, and it's now been a long day and running on the road, so forgive me. Anyway, my mother's sister's cousin-in-law came looking for us to—and told us that the—all the land east of the river Hara had been—was no longer defended, and to flee.

DM: So we've been heading south, and then west as soon as we get a little surer. I am worried to stay on the road much longer, travelers. I greatly thank you for your aid, but we cannot travel as fast as you, and we must just press on.

Kenzo: If you make it to Tokra, send word that, that the party, that Kenzo and Delwath and Seeker, Wellby, Riswynn—that we're—that we—that you encountered us on our way to Raven's Hold. Let them know that you saw us.
DM: Thank you, and I won't say stay safe. I won't say stay safe to you as I can't imagine you'll be safe if you're heading north, but…
Kenzo: What do you—your name? What do you go by?
DM: My name. My name is Shani. This is most my family.
Kenzo: Shani, and where, where are you from? Dunmar, Dunmar?

DM: Here, we've, we've raised our goats in the mountains for a generation now. Good grazing, good lands. I wouldn't say precisely of Karawa, as we typically only spend a couple weeks a year there, but I know people in Karawa. My—my aunt's family is there.
Kenzo: Well, Shani, be safe and spread word to any others that you may see on the road to head to Tokra. And hopefully we'll, we'll see you there in safety in the weeks ahead.

DM: I hope so as well. And she like motions for group to head on and, and as they're riding past she turns back and she says, "And if you see any of those creatures, well, I would advise you to run. They are—they are something out of this world. Never seen anything like it." And then rides off into the distance.

before: DM: One or two of them seem to be wounded in some way, like one of them has his arm kind of wrapped in a sling, and the other—another one has like a bandage around her shoulder and like blood on her cheeks. And they're, they're moving as quickly as they can without horses, heading south along the road. And the four in front—or I'll say half dozen in front, or six in front—seem to be on edge, nervous. Like looking around. But they do not see you.
Wellby: Oh, and there's still a little ways down the road from us.
DM: Yeah, you creep to, you know, within a few hundred yards—300 yards, something like that—and you can see all this.
Wellby: I think at that point, I'll just step out into the middle of the road and raise, you know, raise a hand to them in a gesture of greeting and…
Unknown: Non-threateningness.
after: Seeker: Look back at the stack of crates containing rabbits on my horse and think maybe we should have bought one of their goats.
Unknown: That's okay.
Riswynn: Some people shared your slowing things down with the prey strategy.
Unknown: Right.
Kenzo: I…

interactions.title: The book and the maw creatures’ origin
lines: Riswynn: Didn't want to worry them while they were around, but a giant electrical storm seen miles away could be this site of an interdimensional rift that could let creatures from another world through. You mentioned, Seeker, that sort of origin in that book you saw.
Riswynn: Didn't you say your book said they were not from this world?

Seeker: Indeed, the maw creatures. But how they got here? That's a whole other story. It's an interesting hypothesis you're making there, though, about the electrical storm and interdimensional travel. Maybe we should go there.

before: Seeker: Look back at the stack of crates containing rabbits on my horse and think maybe we should have bought one of their goats.
Unknown: That's okay.
Riswynn: Some people shared your slowing things down with the prey strategy.
Unknown: Right.
Kenzo: I…
after: Riswynn: I’m Raven-bound.
Seeker: Of course…
Delwath: Think we go to Raven’s Hold first.
Seeker: Indeed…

Kenzo: Just in general like as we're traveling, you know, Kenzo, Kenzo basically, as soon as we kind of set up camp, just like will settle into like very intense meditation on this topic of, like, you know, especially given recent experiences. You know, just, just trying to ponder the fabric of reality as intensely as possible. Yeah.

interactions.title: A hungry vulture reports movement in the fortress
lines: DM: So as you begin speaking to a vulture, circles down to land and kind of looks at you and says, "Food?"
Seeker: Water. Well, I point it over to one of the hyena guys. So, you're…

DM: Welcome to this, but—so it like walks over and like starts ripping the thing apart and eating for a little bit, and comes back then and says—it was like blood on its face and stuff like that. So black vultures head is all black, and it's, it's got like little strips of blood now sort of coating its feathers. Now it says, "Say again?"
Seeker: Is anything moving in that fortress at the foot of the mountains?
Delwath: Ask it where it's fed most recently.
Wellby: There's a stream that comes out of the fortress, and maybe that's a… Beautiful. Mm.
Seeker: It seems to be single-minded. What have you eaten most recently?
DM: Very hungry. No food. And it sort of points north, that way. I'm—just moving. Just things moving.
DM: It looks sort of confused. No food, nothing. Everything moving, nothing dead.
Seeker: It only eats dead things, right? Have you been to that big storm?
Seeker: You can't fly. Okay, well, thanks. You can have some of our water too, if you want.
DM: It doesn't need much. Mostly just gets water from the blood and things that kills.
Seeker: Okay. Just want to apologize, everybody, for inviting a vulture to breakfast to tell us something, but it’s just hungry.
Riswynn: You talked to the vulture, and all you heard was it was hungry? Because the rest of us didn’t catch that.
Seeker: Oh, I asked—I summarize. Fair point. I was speaking vulture the whole time. But yeah, nothing. Nothing for it to eat in the fortress. But things were moving in there, apparently.
((The party briefly considers ways into the fortress))

Delwath: Can we get a little—it's hard to tell until we get a little closer, right? I doubt there's hundreds of these creatures. I mean, did the vul—did the vulture have any sense of these things moving? You didn't ask it if it was like many, many things?
Seeker: That probably wouldn't have gotten very good numerical answers. Especially about…
DM: A lot of what you got is that it’s—there's very little on the plain. Yeah. It didn't see anything moving on the…
DM: In the fort, sure. But there's nothing dead, there's nothing alive, there's a sort of thing. Which at least implies there's not more bands of these things waiting.

before: Seeker: I should have thought about this first. I was gonna ask you about the storm, but I might ask it about the fortress. Which is—which of the two is closest, closer to us right now, where we are?
DM: That's a good question.
Kenzo: We go back to the other map?

DM: Yeah, let me drag you back to the other. So you're about here. So I would say Raven's Hold is a bit closer. By—not by a lot. No, it's maybe like a day's travel closer, roughly, to Raven's Hold than the storm. So that's hard to say exactly.

Seeker: I want to say something like, "Is anything moving in that castle at the foot of the mountains?" And I can't use like direction words or ask it like, "What's happening?" because what's happening to a vulture is different from what's happening to us, but anything moving should be clear enough.
after: Seeker: Also true.
Delwath: In like killing stuff. And we're like a day and a half from the fort?
Unknown: Yeah.
Delwath: So I think we go as quick as we can there. Yeah, and see what—I mean, once we're in sight of the walls, we can see if it's feasible to climb around, see if we—see what's best.
Riswynn: Or at least one more day at a fast pace and then decide what we’re doing.

interactions.title: Tharandros warns of poisoned water and agrees to warn Karawa
lines: DM: The one who—who seems to be the leader who's, you know, has a—they're wearing sort of like, you know, vests and sort of green decorated clothes and things strapped to their back with like leather satchels and things like that. And the one who sort of rides forward looks around at you all and then, when he sees Delwath, looks kind of—not exactly puzzled, but just kind of doesn't register the dwarves and the halfling, and glances briefly at Kenzo over there. When he sees Delwath, turns to you and says, in good Elvish, "You are a long way from home in a bad land."
DM: I would not linger, were I you.
Delwath: What have you seen to the east?

DM: Sort of looks around at the—at the five of you and your horses and your gear and says, "This land. The water here. Everything to the north has been sickened by demons. We flee now to the west, and hope you have a good supply to drink, as you will not find anything safe to consume north of here."
Delwath: Demons? I describe the maw creature. Did you see such as that?
DM: Perhaps something like that. I have seen—I have seen a presence in the water. I have seen a—a tie, a rope that binds it to another land. I have seen disease and poison.
Delwath: Does anybody else speak Elvish, by the way?
Delwath: We’ll just sort of huddle around.

DM: He sort of looks around briefly and says, "All the infinite imaginings of the world are found somewhere in the great void of the divine. The first of those"—and he sort of leans, points his head over at Kenzo—"to preach hellfire and damnation, to condemn those who do not obey to an eternity in the chaos of torment and pain and violence without reason or purpose… Those who preached and believed that, those of his kind, created the Abyss. And the nightmares of the world now sustain it. That is the land I see at the end of this rope. We will not stay here."
Delwath: I'll tell them that we're—actually, before that, I'll ask if he has much experience of other lands.
Delwath: How long do centaurs live?
DM: A few hundred years, maybe. "Experience, experience is a complicated thing to measure, elf. Would you say you have much experience of other lands?"
Delwath: Delwath looks at—he sort of smiles, sort of like not humored, but like pained sort of sarcastic smile. "Well, yes, I would, in fact."
DM: The shadow you are tethered to, elf, is hardly what I would call experience. There is a much wider world out there. You have seen perhaps a tiny corner.
Delwath: And what do you know of the shadow? You are the first I've met who can even name it. Course, I've been in these barren lands since I returned.

DM: I know little of what haunts you. There are many shadows in this world. Many reflections of this world. Different degrees of dark and light. All I can see is, if you are not careful, this thread will grow to destroy you. And the god you serve.
Kenzo: At this pause in the conversation, Kenzo kind of just raises his hand slightly and says, "Do you speak Dunmari, by chance?" to the centaur. Me.
DM: He turns and he looks at you and he says, "I do talk that tongue. Such sounds strange in my mouth. I hear well."
Kenzo: We're on a journey to, to Raven's Hold. Do you know anything? Do you have—do you have any understanding of what's happening there?
DM: Have you been—I assume Delwath has been translating?
Delwath: A little bit, not—yes, a bit about the Abyss, not the bit about the shadow.
Seeker: Yeah, so the waters are poisoned, and there's some kind of tether to evil dimension.
Kenzo: Do you know what's happening with the lightning storm to the west of here? Have you heard of this?
DM: He sort of looks off at that. Can we see it from here? Like, what direction? Yeah, you can see it from here.
DM: We are heading there. I guess I'll see.
Kenzo: Why are you headed there?
DM: Living not possible. Lands dry. Demons, demons gone, we return.
DM: Like, struggling for word. He says something in Elvish.
DM: That the tether to another—to the other dimension, while that remains, water poison.
Delwath: Is this tether in a place that one could walk to?

DM: A place, perhaps, or a thing, or a creature. The demons of the Abyss, to reach this world, often pull their home with them. I do not know—he's now shifted to Elvish. I can see fire. I can see blood and hunger and blending of flesh. And these things do not come from this land.
Delwath: I'll translate this. And is this tether at Raven's, or further to the north?

DM: We have traveled—we did not travel into the mountains. Poisoned water spreads from Raven's Hold, I believe. Sorry, I just saw your message. Um, so I, I have not—I am not positive. Do you intend to continue north?
Delwath: We are helping the Dunmari. Their defenses have fallen. The boundary of the realm is unguarded, and they fear what might be coming.
DM: Why is this your concern, elf? Their ancestors' ancestors' ancestors created what is coming.
Delwath: They helped me, when I was very weak. I owe them a debt.
Kenzo: Delwath, can you try to understand more about this history that he's referring to about—is he saying that humans have created this, or that the Dunmari specifically…?
Kenzo: Can you try to understand more what he means?
Delwath: Humans imagined the place of punishment for their sins, and so it became.
Seeker: A hell, that’s what you’re talking about?
Kenzo: Tim, like, what are you talking about? Will I understand what he’s talking about? What place of punishment?
DM: I mean, you, you know that gods are created from belief.
DM: And people don't only believe in good things, right? And so, you know, as soon as somebody starts preaching about demons coming to take away the sinners…
Kenzo: They exist. And I mean that—is he referencing historically like a cult that I would know about? Actually, can I do like an Arcana check?
DM: Yeah, you can do an Arcana check, but you get the sense he's referencing, like, long-ago history, not, like, necessarily anything…

DM: Yeah, so, you know, from what you've been able to pick up of this conversation, you—your feeling is that—so, many—it's really only the humans—not exclusively humans, but mostly humans—who have sort of created their own gods, right? Like most other races, like dwarves, were created by gods and don't imagine anything other than what they're—you know, the Bahrâzel, our parents, are, are—same with halflings, right? They, you know…

DM: All the—the other races have this sort of fixed idea, but humans, their imaginations run wild. And so this huge diversity of—of divine creation is generated by their belief and you get the—so what he's referring to is, you know, the fact that humans have imagined many, many things, and so, you know, the—and those things that are imagined strongly enough become real.
Seeker: So, did some human think up…?
Delwath: No, Cha’mutte was a dragon.

DM: Cha'mutte was a dragon. Dragons exist outside of this. This is just like playing like a traditional D&D. There's like the Outer Planes, right? There's like one for each alignment, and there's like the Abyss, there's the Nine Hells, there's Limbo, etc. Which is sort of boring, but Outer Planes are cool. So it's in keeping with the sense that gods are created by belief. So are heaven and hell. But you get the sense that he's, you know, kind of annoyed at humans for imagining this to begin with, you know, aeons ago.
Delwath: It's a grudge probably passed down from centaur to centaur for 10 generations, right? Yeah, longer, it's not—he's not referring to a—an event that happened 60 years ago.

DM: Right, it's just as—just a, you know, creatures like this that perhaps are more directly exposed to both the goods and evils of the other planes are perhaps more prone to kind of look at humans as the cause of these troubles. In a very broad sense, not a very—not a specific sense.
Seeker: But, so just to review the centaurs' motivation here, they've come from somewhere. We don't know where…
Seeker: And they're going to the storm because they think—because they can't live…
DM: They can't live. Water has been…
Delwath: Is, is the poison spreading? Spreading west?

DM: 10 days ago it was just, I think, just one small stream. Five days ago it was a few watering holes. And yesterday it was everywhere we stopped. I would say it is growing, yes. Whether without bound or contained in some way, I cannot say.
